note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: CoCoLex mechanism and its evidence against context-aware decoding baselines

nodes.name: LLM hallucination in legal text
nodes.description: LLMs in the legal domain tend to produce hallucinations, text inconsistent with authoritative sources such as case law and statutes, which is risky because law requires strict adherence to sources.

nodes.name: RAG still diverges from context
nodes.description: RAG with regular decoding struggles to effectively integrate retrieved context, so outputs can diverge from the provided context.

nodes.name: CAD does not enforce faithfulness
nodes.description: Context-aware decoding methods like CAD amplify the influence of context by adjusting logits (contrasting probabilities with and without context) but do not explicitly enforce faithfulness to the context.

nodes.name: Legal text is templatized
nodes.description: Legal texts often follow templatized structures and verbatim phrases, motivating token copying from context.

nodes.name: Copy-based decoding
nodes.description: CoCoLex stores the hidden states of all context tokens with their next tokens, computes L2 distance to the current hidden state, converts it to similarity exp(-dist), and aggregates over the top-k most similar context vectors into a copy distribution over the vocabulary; it is training-free and needs no additional forward passes.

nodes.name: Entropy-based confidence score
nodes.description: The model's confidence lambda_t = exp(-normalized entropy of its next-token distribution), smoothed with a running average over a past window, so lower entropy gives higher confidence.

nodes.name: CoCoLex interpolation
nodes.description: CoCoLex's final distribution is p = lambda_t * p_model + (1 - lambda_t) * p_copy, so high confidence relies on the model and low confidence shifts to copying.

nodes.name: CAD/AdaCAD short-form only
nodes.description: CAD and AdaCAD improve correctness and faithfulness on short-text CUAD but reduce fluency and coherence, and on ObliQA, AQuAECHR and CLERC they lower correctness and faithfulness (AlignScore) while improving only ROUGE, so they struggle on long-form generation.

nodes.name: CoLex outperforms prior decoding
nodes.description: CoLex (static-weight copy interpolation) improves faithfulness and correctness over regular decoding, CAD and AdaCAD, with larger gains in long-range tasks, and keeps fluency and coherence comparable to regular decoding.

nodes.name: CoCoLex best overall
nodes.description: CoCoLex further improves correctness and faithfulness over CoLex and improves fluency and coherence relative to CoLex, with results mostly statistically significant (e.g. CLERC Mistral Cor-AS 58.12 vs 54.94 CoLex vs 42.38 regular; Wilcoxon, 95%).

nodes.name: Human evaluation favors CoCoLex
nodes.description: On 25 AQuAECHR questions rated by a legal expert on a 5-point scale, CoCoLex scores higher than Regular and AdaCAD on correctness (4.64), faithfulness (4.44), fluency (4.96) and coherence (4.92), and AdaCAD underperforms Regular on faithfulness (3.84).

nodes.name: Saul benefits most from copying
nodes.description: The legally pre-trained Saul-7B underperforms the generalist Mistral-7B because it struggles to synthesize provided context, but copy-based decoding substantially improves Saul.

nodes.name: Chunking limits retrieval-based context
nodes.description: Retrieving and concatenating passages can disrupt semantics through improper chunking, degrading answer accuracy.

nodes.name: CoCoLex+ copies from whole document
nodes.description: CoCoLex+ extends copying to hidden states of the entire document (encoded in overlapping chunks, each token keeping the state from the chunk with most autoregressive context) while keeping only top-k passages as textual context.

nodes.name: CoCoLex+ improves correctness
nodes.description: CoCoLex+ consistently outperforms CoCoLex in correctness on CLERC and AQuAECHR for both models (e.g. CLERC Saul Cor-AS 44.91 vs 34.95) while keeping fluency and coherence comparable, though AQuAECHR Saul passage faithfulness slightly declines.

nodes.name: AdaCAD combination tracks AdaCAD's strength
nodes.description: Combining AdaCAD with CoCoLex improves results where AdaCAD beats regular decoding (CUAD both models, CLERC Saul) and decreases them where AdaCAD underperforms (CLERC Mistral, AQuAECHR both).

isolated_nodes.name: Inference overhead
isolated_nodes.description: Relative to regular decoding (1.00x) on CUAD, CAD/AdaCAD take about 1.75x, CoLex/CoCoLex 1.49-1.51x, AdaCAD+CoCoLex 2.31x, and CoCoLex+ 1.96x (2.96x on the longer AQuAECHR documents).

isolated_nodes.name: Five legal benchmarks, two LLMs
isolated_nodes.description: Evaluation uses CUAD, OALQA, ObliQA, AQuAECHR and CLERC with Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 and Saul-7B-Instruct-v1, under an oracle-document setting with BM25 retrieval of passages.

isolated_nodes.name: Oracle-document limitation
isolated_nodes.description: Experiments assume oracle documents, so real-world generation quality additionally depends on retrieval accuracy over the whole corpus.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from hallucination and the weakness of CAD-style decoding, through the copy-plus-confidence design, to benchmark results, human evaluation, and extensions (CoCoLex+, combination with AdaCAD).
